summary.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management said it is difficult to model the West Asia situation and fuel price impact.
Private-brand discount to market leaders on apparel (about 40%) to remain at least the same, with a possible wider gap.
Store expansion will not slow; management said it aims to open more stores where practical.
Input inflation (petroleum-linked plastics, polyester, detergent inputs) is starting to flow through; full impact expected in the balance of May and June.
Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.
Working capital cycle expected to stay at FY26 levels, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: Store count 795 at March 2026 after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4); presence in 535 cities after adding 77 cities in FY26.
47 of the 105 FY26 openings were in South India (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka); 5 in Gujarat and 3 in Maharashtra.
Trading area 1.34 crore sq ft at March 2026.
Karnataka store areas reduced in many stores; sales per sq ft has risen and is now in line with the national average, per CFO.
Lease escalation about 15% every three years (about 5% a year), per CFO.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 SSSG acceleration to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST rate cuts, plus extra investment in growth and promotions.
FY26 SSSG of 11% split: 7 points from new customers and transactions, 2 points from more items per customer, 2 points from higher price points.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred to the Board and gave no dividend commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kerala is above average, Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) are in line with the network, and small-format stores match large-format stores on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cleared old spring/summer stock ahead of the April-June season and increased promotions to capture a consumption uptick. The CFO said working capital days are about the same as last year and that is the intended operating level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (petroleum derivatives, plastics, polyester, fabric at 10-11%) reaching shelf prices from May-June, and its effect on SSSG and gross margin.
Q4 gross margin compression linked to promotions; whether promotional intensity stays high into the April-June season.
Geopolitical and crude-price shocks, currency depreciation and possible weak rural demand from a poor monsoon.
Vendor labour and gas availability constraints, which the company says are easing.
Rising competition in apparel from e-commerce and value-fashion players moving into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on private-brand resilience, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to model the West Asia and fuel-price impact and said the coming months could be challenging. It was evasive on dividend policy, deferring to the Board.
key_quotes: So, it is clearly correlated with crude pricing in that sense.
We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country.
So, our pricing is totally consumer -led.
The coming months and quarters could be challenging. I don't know.

adds.what: Store expansion: 25 stores opened in Q4 FY26 (105 in FY26), 795 stores at March 2026; management says expansion will not slow, aims to open more where practical

growth.why: No numerical FY27 revenue guidance; management says store expansion will not slow and Q4 SSSG hit 13.2% on consumption uptick, backed by 795 stores and 105 FY26 openings, but no quantified FY27 targets or capacity timelines were given.
